summary: Viewed all four actual PNGs, including the native 64px cells and supplied nearest-neighbor 3x views. The dark blue canine, pointed ears, long muzzle, red throat and bushy tail remain recognizable on all three backgrounds. Broad upper-left highlights and underside shadows give the standing and running bodies volume. Windup lowers the head and bends the legs; move and attack extend the body; attack opens the jaw and reaches forward with connected forelegs; recover closes the mouth, and hit recoils. Standing feet share the baseline, and the dash retains rear-foot support. No obvious accidental interior transparency holes or detached limbs were visible. Skill preparation, discharge and three residual red clusters form a recognizable sequence; poison has drooping posture and green bubbles, stun has altered ears/head and stars, and sleep has a closed eye and folded silhouette. These are visibly different states, not merely whole-body tints. Rework the ambiguous roar origin and the oversized, poorly separated sleeping body. The roar does touch the mouth/fang area, but its bright lower root competes with that connection. Coordinates below are native cell coordinates and identify repair areas. These still pose previews cannot establish playback timing, actual battle contact, source palette/alpha compliance or literal pxgrid authorship. This is a reviewer recommendation, not the user's selection.

issues.message: The bright horizontal orange cluster at x34-38/y35-37 merges the lower jaw/throat into the lowest roar stroke, while the upper connection touches the fang line around x40-44/y29-30. At 1x this gives the effect competing origins and makes it resemble overlapping angular chevrons. Preserve a dark open-mouth cavity, narrow the lower tongue/root, and make the brightest shared emission root visibly start inside the mouth around x40/y31 before separating into two outward branches. Keep the lower jaw contour readable beneath it.

The broad triangular hump from approximately x10-34/y29-51 and long uninterrupted diagonal highlight read as a folded shell or cloak; the slim torso, haunch and bushy tail cease to be individually readable. In both sleep_a and sleep_b, break this plane with a curved haunch-to-flank shadow boundary and a separately contoured tail curl near x12-25/y51-57. Retain the tucked paws and closed eye, and preserve the same body mass across the breathing pair.

At the notch between tail and rump, the pale back cluster at x17/y32-33 is directly exposed to the background and interrupts the dark contour adjoining the back ridge at y31. Trace a one-pixel dark stepped boundary outside this cluster through the tail-root notch, retaining the highlight inside it. Inspect the matching notch in idle_b and idle_c; do not fill the intentional space around the raised tail.
